classification.difficultyReason: Translate the swimming cycles into a common-multiple calculation, then check length-count parity to ensure simultaneous arrivals are at the same end.

content.prompt: Three swimmers take 28 seconds, 44 seconds and 68 seconds to swim one length of the pool. They start together at the same end and swim continuously back and forth. How long will it be before they are side by side at one end of the pool again?

answer.short:
$5236$ seconds.

The first common multiple of the three lap times gives the simultaneous arrival; each swimmer completes an odd number of lengths.
answer.worked:
Taking a lap to mean one length, first list common multiples of 28 and 44:

$308, 616, 924, 1232, 1540, 1848, 2156, 2464, 2772, 3080, 3388, 3696, 4004, 4312, 4620, 4928, 5236,\ldots$

The first number in this list that is also a multiple of 68 is $5236$.

$$\begin{align*}5236\div28&=187\\5236\div44&=119\\5236\div68&=77\end{align*}$$

All three counts are odd, so the swimmers are together at the opposite end after $5236$ seconds.
